lines.trans: Timur, help me out, I have a problem.
I warned you in advance, after all!
Today the shrimp are not of the first freshness.
They are waiting for me in the back courtyard right now.
Maybe you can talk to them calmly?
Well then everything is fine, we will talk to them right now.
Really, listen, I am in your debt now!
You do not owe me anything, you heard nothing about the shrimp.
Hello, Katya, just do not hang up, listen to me.
In short, I was wrong and I want to apologize.
Come to our restaurant tonight together with Stas.
Alright, we will sit together tonight, my treat!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'правый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wrong / in the wrong').

examples.text: В общем, я был неправ и хочу извиниться.
examples.trans: In short, I was wrong and I want to apologize.

examples.text: Я был неправ и хочу извиниться.
examples.trans: I was wrong and I want to apologize.

examples.text: Признаю, я вчера был совсем неправ.
examples.trans: I admit I was completely wrong yesterday.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Двести лошадей, отличный мотоцикл!
examples.trans: Two hundred horsepower, an excellent motorcycle!

examples.text: У меня в молодости такой мотоцикл был.
examples.trans: I had a motorcycle like that in my youth.

examples.text: Час гоняешь, потом весь день перебираешь.
examples.trans: You ride for an hour, then overhaul it all day.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Подождите, я хотел, чтобы всё прошло мирно.
examples.trans: Wait, I wanted everything to go peacefully.

examples.text: Катя, не слушай его, он хотел получить деньги!
examples.trans: Katya, do not listen to him, he wanted to get money!

examples.text: Да я трогать его не хотел, он меня спровоцировал!
examples.trans: I did not want to touch him, he provoked me!

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'виниться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to apologise', paired with 'извиняться'.

examples.text: В общем, я был неправ и хочу извиниться.
examples.trans: In short, I was wrong and I want to apologize.

examples.text: Я был неправ и хочу извиниться.
examples.trans: I was wrong and I want to apologize.

examples.text: Я же извинился.
examples.trans: I said sorry, didn't I?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'езжать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to come (by transport), to arrive', paired with 'приехать'.

examples.text: Приезжайте сегодня вечером к нам в ресторан вместе со Стасом.
examples.trans: Come to our restaurant tonight together with Stas.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, приезжайте к нам скорее!
examples.trans: Please come to us as quickly as possible!

examples.text: Приезжай вечером.
examples.trans: Come over in the evening.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in the evening', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я вчера вечером была занята.
examples.trans: I was busy last night.

examples.text: Приезжайте сегодня вечером к нам в ресторан вместе со Стасом.
examples.trans: Come to our restaurant tonight together with Stas.

examples.text: Хорошо, посидим вечером, я угощаю!
examples.trans: Alright, we will sit together tonight, my treat!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Двести лошадей, отличный мотоцикл!
examples.trans: Two hundred horsepower, an excellent motorcycle!

examples.text: У меня в молодости такой мотоцикл был.
examples.trans: I had a motorcycle like that in my youth.

examples.text: У меня такой в мастерской стоит.
examples.trans: I have one like that standing in my workshop.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы что, знакомы, это мой отец!
examples.trans: Do you two know each other, this is my father!

examples.text: Иди давай, мы тебя ждём на улице.
examples.trans: Go on then, we are waiting for you outside.

examples.text: Как мы между собой конфликты решаем?
examples.trans: How do we settle conflicts among ourselves?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Приезжайте сегодня вечером к нам в ресторан вместе со Стасом.
examples.trans: Come to our restaurant tonight together with Stas.

examples.text: Привет, батя, мы уже приехали в ресторан.
examples.trans: Hi, pops, we have already arrived at the restaurant.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'together', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Приезжайте сегодня вечером к нам в ресторан вместе со Стасом.
examples.trans: Come to our restaurant tonight together with Stas.

examples.text: Вы так сильно хотите быть вместе.
examples.trans: You want to be together so badly.

examples.text: Нет, живите вместе, совет да любовь!
examples.trans: No, live together in harmony and love!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Хорошо, только у меня там блюдо на кухне.
examples.trans: Alright, only I have a dish in the kitchen.

examples.text: Я подумал, что Катя такая красивая и хорошая.
examples.trans: I thought that Katya is so beautiful and good.

examples.text: Да, неси хорошее мясо и вино хорошее.
examples.trans: Yes, bring good meat and good wine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'сидеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'sit a while', paired with 'сидеть'.

examples.text: Посиди с Викой.
examples.trans: Stay with Vika for a while.

examples.text: Давай посидим в кафе.
examples.trans: Let's sit in a café for a bit.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.en: to treat someone to food or drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'гощать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am treating', paired with 'угостить'.

examples.text: Там поляну надо накрывать и угощать гостей.
examples.trans: There you have to set a generous table and treat the guests.

examples.text: Хорошо, посидим вечером, я угощаю!
examples.trans: Alright, we will sit together tonight, my treat!

examples.text: Почему мы должны угощать кого-то?
examples.trans: Why should we treat anyone?
